note: crane.js:1733-1807, the gun-arm preservation trick through the wind tunnel's ride/blown/fly state machine. Audit's premise partly stale by the time this pass started: `GunArmBones` (a Func<Transform[]> override delegate) and the actual save/restore straddling SetPose/HandsOnEdge were ALREADY present in WindRider.cs (crane.js:1753,1804-1807 — the snapshot/restore loops themselves), just permanently inert because nothing ever assigned the delegate and its own header asserted the bone-selection logic (crane.js:981-992, gunSide/rigArm) had 'NOT exposed through FootController's public surface' blocking it. That assertion did not hold on inspection: FootController.Weapons is already public, FootWeapons already exposes Held/Armed/IsRifleHeld/HeldSide publicly, and Combat.Weapons already has public static, NAME-based pure functions (FindHandBone/FindHandBoneL/FindArmChain/FindArmChainL) — the exact same 'resolve independently every frame, do not read private state' pattern Character/FootWeaponFrame.cs's own header documents for this identical hand-bone question (its point 2). So the real gap was narrower than the audit's framing suggested: NO FootController.cs or Combat/Weapons.cs edit was needed at all (no seam had to be added) — the missing piece was purely WindRider.cs's own ResolveGunArmBones() (new, public static, crane.js:981-992/1746-1752 transcribed literally: foot.held?.obj gates whether to protect anything at all, gunSide picks 'L' only for a rifle slung left, rigArm resolves that side's upper+fore+hand), wired as Tick()'s default when the GunArmBones override is left null. `GunArmBones` itself is kept as an explicit override seam (unchanged from before this pass) rather than removed, since a caller/test may still want to inject a fixed list.
verified: Unity -batchmode -quit -nographics -executeMethod TbilisiFly.Probes.WindGunArmProbe.Run, compared against tools/_probe_windgunarm.mjs via tools/unity_port_check.py: 'compared 15 values across 6 js / 6 cs lines, tol=1e-05 ... PASS - 15 values match to float32 precision'. GUNSIDE (3 cases x 4 fields) proves gunSide(foot)'s decision table (rifle+R, rifle+L, unarmed) matches the JS formula exactly. RESOLVECOUNT proves the REAL WindRider.ResolveGunArmBones (called directly, not a replica) returns exactly 3 bones (upper+fore+hand) when armed on either side and 0/null when unarmed, on a REAL loaded banana.fbx rig driven through WindRider.Tick() across off->ride->blown->fly on a synthetic wing (same fixture CraneProbe.cs/Crane3Probe.cs already use). A 30-frame fly-mode hold with the tracked bone forced to an arbitrary rotation every frame before Tick() showed 0.000000 deg drift for the protected side in both the rifle-right and rifle-left cases. HONEST CAVEAT, found and documented prominently in WindGunArmProbe.cs's own header: that 0-drift reading is NOT currently distinguishing 'protected' from 'nothing tried to move it', because of a PRE-EXISTING, project-wide gap unrelated to this port unit — every character FBX in this checkout (banana/eggplant/toad/elephant) has an EMPTY humanoid bone mapping (`human: []`, animationType:2/Generic; a project-wide grep for `animationType: 3` returns zero hits anywhere), and FootPoses.cs's own Build(rig) hard-gates on rig.IsHumanoid before filling in ANY arm/leg bone — so HandsOnEdge/SetWingGrip are no-ops for every body in a fresh batchmode run today, not only for this test. The unarmed case's maxDriftDeg=0 is this gap, not evidence of correctness. What survives that gap and IS solid: ResolveGunArmBones' bone SELECTION (which bones, which side) is proven directly against the production method, independent of IsHumanoid (it is pure name-matching). Proving the full write-vs-restore race needs a Humanoid-configured body, which is a separate, pre-existing fix outside this unit's scope — flagged here rather than silently worked around. Compile verified clean (EXIT=0, no error CS) across all runs after fixing one real build error found along the way: WindGunArmProbe.cs's first draft called `new FootWeapons()`, but FootWeapons' only constructor takes (IFootBelt, Transform) — fixed with a minimal no-op StubFootBelt (every method documented as the same valid reduced-fidelity choice IFootBelt.ResyncRide's own doc comment already allows).
